firmwareWizardStep2Body: Hold the BOOTSEL button while you connect it to your computer via USB. Then release the BOOT SEL button
firmwareWizardStep2Body_nano: Hold the "B" button (the boot button) while you turn the robot back on by pressing the red toggle switch. Then release the boot button.
firmwareWizardStep3Body: Click the button below and pick the drive named {{ drive }} (or your board’s USB drive) so the app can write firmware.uf2. If your browser asks for permission to view or edit files on the drive, choose Edit files or Allow.

firmwareWizardNoFolder: Choose the boot drive folder first.
firmwareWizardNoFolderPicker: Your browser does not support choosing a folder. Try Chrome or Edge.

firmwareWizardSuccessBluetoothReset: Because MicroPython was updated, reset the XRP or power it completely off and back on before Bluetooth will connect.

updateAvailableNeedUsb: Connect your XRP with a USB cable to update firmware or the library.

update-mp-instructions: When the folder selection dialog comes up, select the {{ drive }} drive in the file browser, then click 'OK'. When ask for permission to save, click 'View files' and 'Save Changes'. The update process will take a few minutes. Please do not disconnect the USB cable during this time.

update-lib-instructions: The update process will take a few minutes. Please do not disconnect the USB cable until the process is complete.

update-lib-complete: The XRP library update process has completed successfully.
no-editor-run: Please select a tab with code before pressing Run.
program-not-saved-to-xrp: This program has not been saved to the XRP. Please save it to the XRP before running.
login-desc: The user mode is currently configured to Google User. Please login to your Google Account to edit your files. Click the Google Sign In Button below.
driver-install-desc: The list below shows third party drivers that can be installed on the XRP. Please select the desired drivers and click the 'Install Driver' button to begin the installation process. Note that your XRP must be connected before installing any drivers.

switchToBluetoothStep3: When your browser asks, pick XRP-{{id}} from the list and click Pair. It will remember your XRP until you reload the page.
bleReconnectFailed: Couldn't find XRP-{{id}}. Is it on and in range?
bleConnectCancelled: To connect to XRP-{{id}}, make sure the XRP is powered on with fresh or fully charged batteries, then try again. Or connect an XRP via the USB cable to set a new default XRP.
bleSwitchUsbStillConnected: XRP-{{id}} is still connected by USB. Unplug the USB cable before continuing.
bleWrongUsbXrp: The XRP on the USB cable is XRP-{{otherId}}, not your saved XRP-{{id}}. Choose Bluetooth Connection to connect to XRP-{{id}}, or USB Connection to use XRP-{{otherId}} instead.

pythonSnippets.title: Code
pythonSnippets.hint: Click a snippet to see how it works. Add it, or drag it into your code.

xrp_straight_effort.title: Drive straight
xrp_straight_effort.text: Drives straight for 20 cm at half power. Use a negative distance to go backwards.

xrp_turn_effort.title: Turn
xrp_turn_effort.text: Turns the robot 90 degrees on the spot. Use a negative angle to turn the other way.

xrp_seteffort.title: Set wheel power
xrp_seteffort.text: Sets the power of the left and right wheels, from -1 (full backwards) to 1 (full forwards).

xrp_arcade.title: Drive like a controller
xrp_arcade.text: Drives like a game controller: the first number goes forwards, the second one turns.

xrp_getleftencoder.title: Left wheel distance
xrp_getleftencoder.text: How far the left wheel has turned, in centimetres.

xrp_getrightencoder.title: Right wheel distance
xrp_getrightencoder.text: How far the right wheel has turned, in centimetres.

xrp_motor_effort.title: Motor power
xrp_motor_effort.text: Sets the power of one motor, from -1 to 1. Change the 1 to pick another motor.

xrp_motor_speed.title: Motor speed
xrp_motor_speed.text: Makes one motor spin at a steady speed, in turns per minute.

xrp_motor_get_position.title: Motor turns
xrp_motor_get_position.text: How many turns the motor has made.

xrp_motor_reset_position.title: Reset motor turns
xrp_motor_reset_position.text: Sets the motor's turn counter back to zero.

xrp_servo_deg.title: Move servo
xrp_servo_deg.text: Moves the servo arm to 90 degrees (from 0 to 180).

xrp_getsonardist.title: Distance
xrp_getsonardist.text: The distance to the nearest thing in front of the robot, in centimetres.

xrp_l_refl.title: Left line sensor
xrp_l_refl.text: How much light the left line sensor sees back: 0 is white, 1 is black.

xrp_r_refl.title: Right line sensor
xrp_r_refl.text: How much light the right line sensor sees back: 0 is white, 1 is black.

xrp_yaw.title: Direction
xrp_yaw.text: Which way the robot is facing, in degrees.

xrp_led_on.title: Light on
xrp_led_on.text: Turns on the light on the robot's board.

xrp_led_off.title: Light off
xrp_led_off.text: Turns off the light on the robot's board.

xrp_button_pressed.title: Button pressed?
xrp_button_pressed.text: True while the button on the board is pressed.

xrp_wait_for_button_press.title: Wait for the button
xrp_wait_for_button_press.text: Waits until someone presses the button on the board.

if.title: If
if.text: Runs the code inside only when the condition is True. Replace True with a question.

ifElse.title: If / else
ifElse.text: Runs the first part when the condition is True, and the part under else when it is not.

compare.title: Compare
compare.text: A question that is True or False. You can also use >, <=, >=, == and !=.

whileTrue.title: Repeat for ever
whileTrue.text: Repeats the code inside for ever.

forRange.title: Repeat 4 times
forRange.text: Repeats the code inside 4 times. i counts 0, 1, 2, 3.

xrp_sleep.title: Wait
xrp_sleep.text: Waits half a second before the next line.

randomInt.title: Random number
randomInt.text: A random whole number from 1 to 10.

print.title: Show a message
print.text: Shows a message in the Terminal.

comment.title: Note
comment.text: A note for people reading the code. The robot skips lines that start with #.

variable.title: Variable
variable.text: Keeps a value under a name, so you can use it again and change it in one place.

function.title: Function
function.text: Gives a name to some steps. Write my_function() to run them.

archived.title: Archived projects
archived.hint: Projects you put away to keep your list tidy. They are safe here: nothing is deleted. Bring one back whenever you want.
